catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acoemetae: A 1913 entry on the Acoemetae — the sleepless monks of Constantinople. Joseph Sollier tells of their endless psalmody. Day and night the chant never ceased. Prayer without pause, in relays. Their abbots quarreled with emperors and patriarchs. The Studion inherited their fervor.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acta-sanctoru: This 1913 reference piece on the Acta Sanctorum Hiberniae — Colgan's great lives of the Irish saints. William Grattan-Flood honors the Louvain Franciscan. His folios saved Ireland's holy memory. A monument of Irish scholarship. His manuscripts survive in Dublin and Rome. Irish hagiography starts with Colgan.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acta-triadis-: A 1913 entry on the Acta Triadis Thaumaturgae — Colgan's lives of Patrick, Brigid, and Columba. William Grattan-Flood praises the wonder-working three. Ireland's three great patrons in one volume. Hagiography's Irish crown. Patrick's bell and Brigid's fire live in its pages. The three guard Ireland still.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ad-universali: A 1913 entry on the papal constitution Ad Universalis Ecclesiae — its occasion, contents, and force. P.M.J. Rock explains the document. Rome's governing voice, in formal dress. Church law at its most solemn. Its clauses shaped diocesan life. Canonists cite it to this day.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-advocatus-ecc: A 1913 entry on the advocatus ecclesiae — the lay protector of church lands. Johann Peter Kirsch traces the medieval office. Vogts guarded abbeys with the sword. The post grew into princely power. Protection that became lordship. The office faded with feudalism's fall.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agapetae: This 1913 reference piece on the agapetae — the beloved ones, virgins dwelling with clerics. John Joseph A'Becket tells the scandal. Councils condemned the dangerous custom. Charity's name covered folly. A dark page of early discipline. Jerome's letters thunder against the abuse.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agnoetae: This 1913 reference article on the Agnoetae — the heretics who denied Christ's full knowledge. The entry traces their error and fall. Themistius led their doubting school. The Church held Christ's perfect wisdom. A sixth-century battle of ideas. Their error died with its teacher.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amphorae: This 1913 reference piece on amphorae — the great jars of the ancients. Maurice Hassett describes their sacred use. Wine and oil filled their bellies. The catacombs yield them still. The pantry of the old world. Their stamps date the ancient cargoes.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ampullae: A 1913 entry on ampullae — the little pilgrim flasks. Maurice Hassett tells their holy use. They carried oil from martyrs' shrines. Monza keeps the famous set. Devotion's small vessels. Their tin kept the holy oil. Their shapes please the museum visitor.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amyclae: This 1913 reference piece on Amyclae — the old town of Latium. The entry preserves its scanty record. Virgil sang its silent marshes. The pastures keep its ancient name. A name in the Latin story. Its silence gave the proverb birth. Its fields are quiet now.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apostolicae-c: A 1913 entry on Apostolicae Curae — Leo XIII's bull on Anglican orders. Michael O'Riordan explains its grave verdict. The orders were declared null. The bull closed the long debate. Rome's final word of 1896. Its Latin is the curia's finest. Its verdict stands to this day.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arcae: A 1913 entry on Arcae — Arqa, the Phoenician city, now a titular see. Thomas Shahan notes its Christian past. The Crusaders prized its fortress. The Church keeps its ancient name. A see of the Levantine coast. Its citadel crowned the coastal hill.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arsacidae: A 1913 entry on the Arsacidae — the Parthian kings of the East. Jérôme Labourt tells their long reign. They faced Rome for four centuries. The Christians lived under their rule. The dynasty of the eastern frontier. Their capital was Ctesiphon's glory.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-augilae: This 1913 reference article on Augilae — Aujila, the oasis city, now a titular see. Thomas Shahan notes its desert past. Its bishops grace the old lists. The Sahara guards its palms. A see of the Libyan sands. Its dates fed the desert caravans.
